course_title_en: Mongolian and English Step by Step

units.scope: greetings, names, thanks; сайн байна уу, та vs чи; EN: I am / you are, my name is

lessons.focus: Meeting someone in the street or at school; сайн байна уу, сайн уу, баяртай, өглөөний мэнд, оройн мэнд; EN: Hello/Hi, Good morning/evening, Goodbye

lessons.title_en: Formal and Informal: Та and Чи
lessons.focus: Greeting an elder versus a friend in Ulaanbaatar; how are you (сайн уу, сайхан байна уу); та vs чи and when to use each; EN: you are / I am (to be) with How are you? I'm fine
Introducing yourself at a new class or party; нэр, миний нэр ... бөгөөд ..., таны нэр хэн бэ; EN: My name is..., What's your name?, I am + name
Meeting a new person and exchanging basic info; танилцъя, танилцсандаа баяртай байна, найз, багш, оюутан; EN: Nice to meet you, he/she is, this is my friend
Polite exchanges in a shop or on a bus; баярлалаа, зүгээр, уучлаарай, үгүй/тиймээ, гуйя; EN: Thank you, You're welcome, Sorry, Excuse me, please
A full first-meeting dialogue at a friend's home or at work; combine greetings, та/чи, names, thanks; EN: review of I am / you are / my name is in short conversations

units.scope: Cyrillic alphabet, ө/ү, long vowels; intro to vowel harmony; EN: alphabet, spelling names aloud

lessons.focus: Seeing signs and brand names in Ulaanbaatar; Cyrillic letters that look and sound like English ones (а, о, э, к, м, т, н) with simple words like мама, кофе, такси; EN: first half of the alphabet A-M, saying letter names

Reading street names and shop signs; false-friend letters (в, н, р, с, у, х, ы, ь, ъ) and Cyrillic-only consonants (ж, ш, ч, ц, щ, я, ю, ё, е); EN: second half of the alphabet N-Z, confusing letter names

lessons.title_en: The Special Letters Ө and Ү
lessons.focus: Pronouncing Mongolian words correctly on the phone and at a market; ө and ү versus о and у with pairs like хол/хөл, ус/үс; EN: vowel sounds and spelling with minimal pairs (ship/sheep) as a parallel

Listening and repeating everyday words where length changes meaning; doubled vowels аа, оо, уу, өө, үү, ээ and ий; words like ах/аав, нар/наар; EN: stress and long/short sounds, e.g. reading words like cat, name, tree

Adding endings to simple nouns while talking about home and city; back (а, о, у) versus front (э, ө, ү) vowels, e.g. ном-д / гэр-т / сургууль-д; EN: plural -s and sound variations (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/), noticing patterns in word endings

Introducing yourself at a hotel desk or on the phone and spelling your name aloud; reading and writing Mongolian and foreign names in Cyrillic (Болд, Сарнай, Майкл); Танай нэрийг хэрхэн бичдэг вэ?; EN: How do you spell...?, spelling names aloud with letter names

units.scope: classroom and everyday objects; энэ/тэр, question particles вэ/бэ, уу/үү; EN: this/that, a/an, What is...?

lessons.focus: Pointing at things on a classroom desk; core objects (ном, үзэг, харандаа, дэвтэр, цүнх); энэ юу вэ? / Энэ ном. with EN: This is a book, What is this?
Asking about things far from you in a classroom; board, chair, table, window, door; тэр vs энэ with EN: this vs that, What is that?
Checking what things are in a shop or at home; phone, key, cup, bag; уу/үү and тийм/үгүй answers with EN: Is this a ...? Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.
Naming items in a bag, with vowel-initial words; apple, umbrella, egg, orange, book; уу/үү choice questions with EN: a vs an.
Identifying people and things in a room or photo; teacher, student, friend, computer, picture; вэ vs бэ after the final sound, хэн бэ with EN: What is...? Who is...?
Describing a room and a classroom in a short dialogue; mixed everyday objects review; combining энэ/тэр, вэ/бэ, уу/үү with EN: this/that, a/an, plural these/those preview with is/are.

units.scope: family members; миний/таны, possessive минь/чинь; EN: my/your/his/her, have, plural -s

lessons.focus: Naming the closest family members (ээж, аав, ах, эгч, дүү, хүү, охин); EN: my/your with family nouns; MN: миний and таны before a noun (миний ээж, таны аав)
Showing a family photo to a friend; extended family (өвөө, эмээ, нагац ах, авга эгч, үеэл); EN: his/her with family nouns; MN: түүний for he/she, and ах/эгч/дүү as age-based terms
Telling a new classmate who is in your family; siblings and children; EN: have/has (I have, she has); MN: possession with dative-locative and байна (надад ах байна, танд дүү байна уу?)

lessons.title_en: How Many Are in Your Family?
lessons.title_mn: Танай гэр бүлд хэн хэн бий вэ?
lessons.focus: Describing family size at a Ulaanbaatar family dinner; numbers with family members; EN: plural -s and irregular plurals (brother/brothers, child/children); MN: хэдэн + noun, no plural needed after numbers, and -нар for people
Talking warmly about family and sharing small details like names and jobs; EN: possessive 's (my mom's name); MN: possessive minь/чинь (ээж минь, аав чинь) for affection and closeness

Introducing the whole family in a short talk or message; review of family vocabulary; EN: combining my/your/his/her, have, and plurals in short descriptions; MN: манай/танай (our/your family) and linking short sentences

units.scope: numbers 1-100, age, phone numbers; хэд, хэдэн нас; EN: How old are you?, number words

lessons.focus: Counting on your fingers and at a market stall; numbers нэг to арав (нэг, хоёр, гурав, дөрөв, тав, හ зургаа, долоо, найм, ес, арав) and zero тэг; EN: number words one to ten and their spelling, How many? with hэдэн
Reading house numbers and bus numbers; teens арван нэг…хорин and tens (гуч, дөч, тавь, жар, далан, наян, ер); EN: teen vs ty number words (13/30, 15/50) and stress contrast
Reading prices and page numbers on a bus or in a shop; combining tens and units (хорин таван, гучин долоо), 100 зуу; EN: building compound numbers such as twenty-five with a hyphen
Asking and telling age when meeting new friends; хэдэн нас, надад ... нас, би ... настай; EN: How old are you? I am ... (years old), he/she is ...
Talking about the ages of parents, siblings and children at a family gathering; ... настай, ахмад/бага, төрсөн өдөр хэзээ вэ; EN: his/her age, older/younger, my birthday is... (basic use)
Exchanging phone numbers when making a new friend; утасны дугаар хэд вэ, digit-by-digit reading, дугаараа хэлээч; EN: What's your phone number? saying digits aloud, double and 'oh' for zero

units.scope: countries, nationalities, languages; ablative -аас/-ээс/-оос/-өөс; EN: be from, capitalized nationalities

lessons.focus: Looking at a world map and naming countries; vocabulary: Mongolia, China, Russia, Korea, Japan, USA, Germany, France, England, Kazakhstan; grammar: Mongolian country names as proper nouns and EN capitalized country names, 'This is...' / Энэ ... байна

Meeting a new person at a hostel in Ulaanbaatar and asking about origin; vocabulary: хаанаас, хот, орон, Монгол, Улаанбаатар, Эрдэнэт, Дархан; grammar: ablative -аас/-ээс/-оос/-өөс with vowel harmony (Би Монголоос), EN: I am from / Where are you from?

Introducing yourself and others at a university orientation; vocabulary: Монгол хүн, Америк хүн, Хятад хүн, Солонгос хүн, Япон хүн, Орос хүн; grammar: country + хүн for nationality, EN: He is American / She is Korean, capitalized nationalities

Talking about languages at an international party; vocabulary: монгол хэл, англи хэл, орос хэл, хятад хэл, солонгос хэл, ярих, мэдэх; grammar: Би ... хэлээр ярьдаг, instrumental -аар/-ээр for language, EN: I speak English, capitalized language names

Chatting about hometowns, city vs countryside; vocabulary: хот, аймаг, сум, нутаг, том, жижиг, Хөвсгөл, Архангай, Дорнод; grammar: ablative with places and 'from ... to' (-аас ... -руу), EN: He/She is from..., Is he from...? / Where is she from?

Review dialogue at a multicultural gathering, introducing friends; vocabulary: найз, оюутан, танилцъя, уулзсандаа баяртай байна, mixed countries and languages; grammar: combine ablative, nationality and language sentences, EN: be from, negatives with isn't/aren't from

units.scope: buuz, milk tea, basic foods; accusative -ыг/-ийг, present-future -на/-нэ/-но/-нө; EN: like/want, some, uncountable nouns

lessons.focus: Naming common foods at a family table; vocabulary: бууз, хуушуур, мах, талх, будаа, шөл, архи-free staples like сүү, цай; grammar: EN a/an vs uncountable nouns (bread, rice, meat are not counted), MN plain noun phrases like 'Энэ бууз' without articles

Drinks at home and in a café; vocabulary: сүүтэй цай, ус, кофе, жүүс, айраг, архи excluded, шар айраг excluded; grammar: EN some with uncountable nouns (some tea, some water), MN asking and offering with уу/үү (Цай уу?)

Saying what you like and want to eat; vocabulary: дуртай, хүсэх, амттай, амтгүй; grammar: EN like/want + noun (I like buuz. I want some tea.), MN дуртай pattern 'Би бууз дуртай' with dative-style 'бууzд дуртай' introduced simply as set phrase 'Би бууzд дуртай'
Describing what you eat and drink now or later; vocabulary: идэх, уух, хийх, авах; grammar: MN present-future -на/-нэ/-но/-нө with vowel harmony (иднэ, уунa, авна), EN present simple I eat / I drink

Shopping for ingredients at a market; vocabulary: төмс, лууван, сонгино, байцаа, талх, өндөг, мах; grammar: MN accusative -ыг/-ийг/-г/-ийг after vowels and consonants (Мах авна → Махыг авна), EN object after verb with some (I want some potatoes)

Offering food politely to guests in a ger and accepting or refusing; vocabulary: ав, уугаарай, идээрэй, баярлалаа, хангалттай; grammar: review of accusative + -на/-нэ with offers (Цай уух уу? Бууз идэх үү?), EN Would you like some...? / Yes, please. / No, thank you.

units.scope: rooms, furniture, the ger; dative-locative -д/-т, байна; EN: there is/are, in/on/under

lessons.focus: showing a friend around an apartment in Ulaanbaatar; rooms (өрөө, унтлагын өрөө, зуух, угаалгын өрөө, зочны өрөө, хонгил); simple байна for existence and EN: There is a... / There are two...
describing what is in a room; furniture (ор, ширээ, сандал, шүүгээ, диван, зурагт, цонх, хаалга); asking and answering Энд юу байна вэ? / EN: Is there a...? Are there any...? and short answers

lessons.title_en: Where Is It? In, On, Under
lessons.title_mn: Хаана байна вэ? Дотор, дээр, доор
lessons.focus: finding lost things at home (keys, phone, bag); location words дотор, дээр, доор, хажууд, өмнө, ард; dative-locative -д/-т (ширээн дээр, шүүгээнд) with Хаана байна вэ?; EN: in/on/under/next to + Where is...?

visiting a family's ger in the countryside; ger parts and items (тооно, унь, хана, бааган, хоймор, голомт, төв, ор, сав); layout with -д/-т and байна (гэрийн төвд тогоо байна); EN: there is/are with in/on/under/in the middle

comparing where people live: ger district, apartment, house, countryside; орон сууц, байшин, гэр хороолол, хөдөө; living in a place with -д/-т (Улаанбаатарт, хөдөө, гэрт амьдардаг); also байхгүй for absence; EN: There isn't/aren't, live in + place

describing your own home to a new friend, review project; combine rooms, furniture, location and -д/-т with байна, байхгүй; short connected description of 4-6 sentences; EN: There is/are, in/on/under, My home has...

units.scope: daily routine, clock time; habitual -даг/-дэг/-дог/-дөг; EN: present simple, third-person -s, at + time

lessons.focus: Getting up and starting the day; morning verbs (wake up, get up, wash, eat breakfast, drink tea); EN: present simple with I/you/we/they, e.g. I get up early; MN: stems of daily verbs (босох, угаах, идэх, уух) with habitual -даг/-дэг/-дог/-дөг for 'I usually...', e.g. Би өглөө эрт босдог
Asking and telling time; o'clock, half past, quarter past, minutes; EN: What time is it?, at + time; MN: цаг, минут, хагас, past-the-hour patterns, Хэдэн цагт? with dative-locative -т (7 цагт)

Commute and daytime routine; go to school/work, take the bus, study, work, have lunch; EN: present simple with at + time in full sentences (I go to school at eight); MN: habitual -даг/-дэг/-дог/-дөг with time phrases and places, e.g. Би 8 цагт автобусаар сургуульд явдаг

Describing other people's routines (my mother, my brother); family routines; EN: third-person -s (works, goes, studies, watches); MN: habitual forms for third person, same ending for all persons, Ээж маань өглөө эрт босдог; contrast with English agreement

Evening routine; cook dinner, watch TV, read, do homework, go to bed; EN: negatives and questions in present simple (don't/doesn't, Do you...?, Does she...?); MN: negative habitual -даггүй/-дэггүй/-доггүй/-дөггүй and questions with уу/үү (Та орой телевиз үздэг үү?)

Review: describing a full day from morning to night; frequency words (always, usually, sometimes, never; үргэлж, ихэвчлэн, заримдаа, хэзээ ч); EN: adverbs of frequency with present simple, sequence words (then, after that); MN: combining habitual sentences with дараа нь, 'тэгээд', and frequency adverbs, e.g. Би ихэвчлэн 7 цагт босдог

units.scope: city places, buses, directions; хаана, -руу/-рүү, instrumental -аар/-ээр; EN: to/at, imperatives

lessons.focus: Naming places in Ulaanbaatar from a city walk; bank, school, hospital, market, park, shop, station, Sukhbaatar Square; this/that is a... with the pattern 'Энэ ... мөн үү?' and English 'It's a/the ...'

Asking a passerby where a place is; location words (near, far, next to, opposite, in front of); хаана байна вэ? with 'Where is...?' and 'at/in' for location (Банк хаана байна вэ? - Банк зах дээр байна)
Saying where you are going on a normal day; verbs явах, очих, ирэх; directional -руу/-рүү with хаашаа?; English 'go to' vs 'be at/in'
Getting around by bus, taxi, trolleybus, on foot; bus stop, fare, line number, ticket; instrumental -аар/-ээр/-оор/-өөр for transport (автобусаар, таксигаар, явганаар); English 'by bus/on foot'
Giving and following street directions; left, right, straight, corner, crossroads, traffic light; imperatives in Mongolian (яв, эргэ, өнгөр) and English (Turn left, Go straight, Stop)
Review dialogue: a visitor asks for directions and the best way to travel to a place; combining хаана, -руу/-рүү, -аар/-ээр, imperatives; 'Excuse me, how do I get to...?', Уучлаарай, ... яаж очих вэ?

units.scope: prices, tögrög, buying things; хэд вэ, polite -аарай/-ээрэй, -өөч; EN: How much, Can I have, these/those

lessons.focus: Walking into a shop or the Narantuul market and naming what is sold (талх, сүү, жимс, ус, дэвтэр, гар утас); store vocabulary: дэлгүүр, зах, худалдагч, үйлчлүүлэгч; grammar: энэ юу вэ? / Танд ... байна уу? and English 'Do you have...?' and 'I need...'

Asking a price at a market stall; numbers in hundreds and thousands, төгрөг (мянга, сая); grammar: Энэ хэд вэ? / Хэдэн төгрөг вэ? and English 'How much is it? / How much are they?', 'It is 5,000 tögrög'

Pointing at several items on a shelf and comparing them (cheap, expensive: хямд, үнэтэй); demonstratives эдгээр/тэдгээр with plural forms; grammar: English this/that vs these/those with plural nouns, 'These apples are cheap'

Asking a seller for items politely at the counter (a kilo of potatoes, two bottles of water, a bag); quantities and measures: кг, шил, боодол, ширхэг; grammar: polite request -өөч/-ээч/-аач (өгөөч) and English 'Can I have...?', 'Please'

Being polite with a shopkeeper: choosing, taking, waiting, and paying (cash, card, change: бэлэн мөнгө, карт, хinvolved in the exchange); grammar: polite imperative -аарай/-ээрэй/-оорой/-өөрэй (аваарай, орж ирээрэй) and English 'Here you are', 'Thank you', 'Here's your change'

lessons.title_en: At the Store: Putting It Together
lessons.focus: Full shopping dialogue: greeting, asking for items, asking prices, taking some, paying, saying thanks; mixed vocabulary review (food, clothes, school items) with total price; grammar review: хэд вэ, -өөч, -аарай/-ээрэй and English How much, Can I have, these/those

units.scope: days, months, seasons, cold winters; adjectives, negation -гүй and биш; EN: it is cold, isn't/aren't, adjective + noun

lessons.focus: Talking about which day it is and what day tomorrow is; Даваа, Мягмар, Лхагва, Пүрэв, Баасан, Бямба, Ням; Өнөөдөр ... гараг байна / Today is ...; EN: It is + day, on + day

Saying which month and season it is and when your birthday is; нэгдүгээр сар–арван хоёрдугаар сар, хавар, зун, намар, өвөл; Одоо ... улирал/сар байна / It is spring, in June; EN: in + month/season, It is + month

Describing today's weather in Ulaanbaatar and the countryside; хүйтэн, дулаан, халуун, салхитай, бороотой, цастай, нарлаг; Өнөөдөр цаг агаар ямар вэ? / It is cold, hot, windy; EN: How is the weather? It is + adjective

Comparing seasons and places and describing things around you; том, жижиг, шинэ, хуучин, сайхан, урт, богино; adjective before noun (хүйтэн өвөл) vs. predicate adjective; EN: adjective + noun, a cold winter, a big city

Correcting statements about weather and days (It isn't Monday; the weather isn't bad); биш with nouns and adjectives (Энэ Даваа биш), Yes/No answers тийм/үгүй; EN: isn't/aren't, negative short answers

Weather reports and weekend plans with what is missing or not present; -гүй suffix (цасгүй, салхигүй, бороогүй, халуун биш), choosing -гүй vs биш; EN: review of isn't/aren't, there is no..., adjective + noun in short weather reports

units.scope: weekend activities; past -сан/-сэн, -лаа/-лээ; EN: past simple, regular and irregular verbs

lessons.focus: Asking a friend about the weekend on Monday morning; core weekend verbs (go, rest, sleep, watch, cook, clean); Mongolian past -сан/-сэн/-сон/-сөн with vowel harmony in statements and юу хийсэн бэ?; English past simple of regular verbs (-ed: watched, cleaned, cooked, rested, visited)

Telling about a Saturday visit to grandparents or relatives, including a ger district or the countryside; family and visiting vocabulary (visit, help, talk, drink tea, eat buuz, play with kids); -сан/-сэн with dative-locative and comitative (-тай/-тэй) in past sentences; English regular past spelling and pronunciation (-ed as /t/, /d/, /ɪd/: visited, helped, played)

Describing a day out in the city (Sükhbaatar Square, a mall, the cinema); movement and everyday action verbs (go, come, see, buy, eat, meet, take a bus); Mongolian past with common irregular-looking stems and -сан/-сэн forms after vowel-final and consonant-final stems; English common irregular verbs (went, saw, ate, bought, met, came)

Reporting something that just happened or was done by the speaker, such as calling a friend or finishing the laundry; household chores and quick actions (wash, call, finish, write, open); Mongolian past -лаа/-лээ/-лоо/-лөө vs -сан/-сэн (immediate or witnessed vs general past); English past simple with time words (yesterday, last night, ago, this morning)

Explaining what you did not do because of weather, work, or tiredness; reasons and weekend plans that fell through (stay home, be busy, be tired, rain); Mongolian past negation -сангүй/-сэнгүй and болоогүй/-аагүй forms in simple sentences; English didn't + base verb and was/were/wasn't/weren't

Telling and asking about a whole weekend in order, with a friend or in a short message; sequence words and weekend review vocabulary (first, then, after that, in the evening, Saturday, Sunday); mixing -сан/-сэн, -лаа/-лээ and negation in a short narrative, with Хаана? Хэзээ? Хэнтэй? questions; English Did you...? questions with short answers (Yes, I did / No, I didn't) and wh-questions in the past

units.scope: hobbies, sports, music; -х дуртай, чадна; EN: like + -ing, can/can't

lessons.title_en: What Do You Like to Do?
lessons.focus: Two friends chat about free time (чөлөөт цаг); core hobby verbs such as reading, cooking, walking, drawing, watching movies; the pattern -х дуртай (Би унших дуртай) and EN like + -ing (I like reading)

Talking about sports at school or in the park; football, basketball, volleyball, swimming, skiing, table tennis, and play vs do/go in English; likes and dislikes with -х дуртай / -х дургүй and EN like/love/hate + -ing

Sharing favorite music at a café or concert; morin khuur, guitar, piano, singing, songs, genres, throat singing (хөөмий); asking Ямар хөгжим сонсох дуртай вэ? and answering with -х дуртай; EN: What kind of music do you like? I like listening to...

Telling what you can do at a talent show or in a new club; skills such as swimming, riding a horse, singing, cooking, playing chess; чадна and чадахгүй, with -х чадвартай as an alternative; EN: can/can't for ability (I can swim, She can't ride a horse)

Asking about ability and how well someone does things; games and traditions such as chess, shagai (ankle-bone game), cards, and riding; questions with чадах уу? and short answers (Тийм, чадна / Үгүй, чадахгүй); adverbs well/badly/a little (сайн, муу, жаахан); EN: Can you...? Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

Choosing a hobby club at university or a community center and describing your free time; reviewing hobby, sport, and music vocabulary; combining -х дуртай and чадна (Би гитар тоглох дуртай, гэхдээ сайн чадахгүй); EN: combining like + -ing with can/can't, plus and/but

units.scope: body parts, symptoms, pharmacy; progressive -ж/-ч байна, өвдөж байна; EN: present continuous, have a headache

lessons.focus: telling a friend you feel unwell; main body parts (толгой, гэдэс, нуруу, хоолой, шүд, нүд, чих); introducing өвдөж байна / өвдөнө pattern with body part + өвдөж байна; EN: my head/stomach/back hurts, have a headache/stomachache/toothache

lessons.title_mn: Та одоо юу хийж байна вэ?
lessons.focus: describing what people are doing right now at home or in a waiting room; common action verbs (ном унших, ус уух, амрах, унтах, ярих); progressive -ж/-ч байна with regular verbs and the vowel-ending rule (-ж after vowels/most consonants, -ч after л, н, р-type stems); EN: present continuous affirmative (am/is/are + -ing) and spelling of -ing

explaining how you feel to a family member; symptoms (халуурах, ханиалгах, найтаах, толгой эргэх, дотор муухай оргих, ядрах); negative and question forms: -ж байна уу?, -ж байгаа юм биш, байхгүй; EN: present continuous negatives and questions (Are you coughing? I'm not sleeping well), feel + adjective

registering at a clinic and talking to the doctor; clinic vocabulary (эмч, эмнэлэг, цаг авах, үзлэг, температур, даралт, өвчтөн); doctor's questions Хаана өвдөж байна вэ? Хэдэн өдөр болж байна вэ?; duration with хэдэн өдрөөс; EN: How long have you...? basic duration with for/since in simple use, What's wrong? Where does it hurt?, present continuous for temporary states

buying medicine and understanding instructions; pharmacy words (эм, ундаа, шахмал, түрхэх тос, жор, эмийн сан, өдөрт гурван удаа); polite requests and instructions with -аарай/-ээрэй and хоолны өмнө/дараа; EN: Can I have something for...?, take two tablets, three times a day, before/after meals

phoning in sick and visiting a sick friend; review of health vocabulary and wishes (эдгэрэх, амрах, тусламж хэрэгтэй, өвчтэй байна, ажилдаа очиж чадахгүй байна); combining -ж байна with reasons and wishes; EN: I'm calling because..., I'm staying home, Get well soon, review of present continuous vs present simple for health

units.scope: deel, colors, describing people; comparative -аас илүү; EN: comparatives, wear vs put on

lessons.focus: Getting dressed for the day; basic clothing words (deel, shirt, trousers, shoes, hat, coat, boots); EN: wear + clothing, a pair of; MN: өмсөх and the accusative -ыг/-ийг with clothes, and other verbs for putting on items (өмсөх, углах, зүүх)

Looking at traditional deels at a Tsagaan Sar family gathering; colors (red, blue, green, yellow, white, black, brown, gray); adjective before noun in both languages, e.g. улаан дээл, a blue deel; MN colors as modifiers with no ending

Getting ready to leave on a cold Ulaanbaatar morning; coat, scarf, gloves, hat, boots, belt (бүс); EN: wear (state) vs put on (action), e.g. She is wearing a red scarf / She puts on her coat; MN: өмсөж байна (state) vs өмсөв/өмсөх (action) and the verbs зүүх, углах, өмсөх

Describing a friend or family member to someone; looks (tall, short, young, old, thin, heavy), hair and eyes (урт/богино үс, хар нүд); EN: He/She has + hair/eyes, is + adjective; MN: adjective + хүн, үстэй, нүдтэй, -тай/-тэй for features

lessons.title_mn: Илүү том, илүү хямд, илүү дулаан
lessons.focus: Comparing two coats or deels at a market (Narantuul/shop); adjectives big, small, cheap, expensive, warm, light, heavy; EN: comparative -er and more + adjective, than, irregular better; MN: noun + -аас/-ээс/-оос/-өөс + илүү + adjective (энэ дээл тэр дээлээс илүү дулаан)

lessons.title_mn: Аль нь надад зохиж байна вэ?
lessons.focus: Trying on clothes in a shop with a friend and giving opinions; size, fits, suits (тохирох, зохих), too big/small, prefer; EN: review of comparatives with wear/put on, as ... as, fits/suits; MN: надад том байна, илүү дуртай, аль нь, review of -аас илүү in a dialogue

units.scope: tickets, transport, packing; intention -х гэж байна, future -на; EN: going to, will

lessons.focus: Friends decide where to go on vacation; trip vocabulary (аялал, хөдөө, зуслан, амралт, найз нөхөд); intention with -х гэж байна (Би хөдөө явах гэж байна) and EN: be going to for plans

At the bus or train station ticket counter; тийз, нэг талын/хоёр талын, суудал, цаг, платформ; polite requests and asking times/prices with future -на; EN: will for decisions and offers (I'll take two tickets)

Choosing how to travel (bus, train, minibus, car, plane, hitchhiking); тээвэр, жолооч, буудал, зам, хэдэн цаг явах; instrumental -аар/-ээр with future -на; EN: going to vs will for travel predictions and plans

Packing for a trip to the countryside; цүнх, дулаан хувцас, гутал, шүдний con, нарны шил, цэнэглэгч, малгай, өмд, пальто; listing what you intend to take with -х гэж байна and accusative; EN: going to for packing plans, I'm going to take...

Checking the forecast before leaving and guessing what will happen; бороо орно, салхи салхилна, дулаарна, хүйтэрнэ; future -на for predictions and promises; EN: will for predictions, probably, won't, going to when evidence is present (It's going to rain)

Arriving in the countryside, meeting a host family, talking about the days ahead; гэр, айл, морь унах, зочлох, ирэх долоо хоногт; combining intention -х гэж байна and future -на in a dialogue; EN: contrasting going to and will in a conversation and short review

units.scope: holiday customs, greetings, guests; reflexive possessive -аа/-ээ, comitative -тай/-тэй/-той; EN: ordinals, in/on/at with dates

lessons.focus: Preparing at home before the holiday; vocabulary: Tsagaan Sar, Bituun (New Year's Eve), cleaning, buuz, ul boov, new deel; grammar: reflexive possessive -аа/-ээ/-оо/-өө with family and household nouns (гэрээ цэвэрлэнэ, дээлээ өмсөнө); EN: ordinals 1st-5th and the date pattern 'on + date'

Zolgokh greeting ritual with grandparents and relatives; vocabulary: амар байна уу, золгох, хадаг, хүндэтгэл, ах дүү, ахмад хүн; grammar: reflexive possessive with objects and people (аавдаа, эцэг эхээ, хадгаа барина); EN: ordinals 6th-12th, 'in + month', 'on + date'

Hosting visitors in the ger or apartment; vocabulary: зочин, ширээ, тавгийн цай, сүүтэй цай, архи, хүндлэх, суух; grammar: comitative -тай/-тэй/-той with people (найзтайгаа, хамаатантайгаа золгоно), vowel harmony; EN: 'with' and ordinals 13th-20th, 'at + time of the visit'

Describing the traditional spread; vocabulary: өндөр шөл, овсон, шийстэй хонины ястай, цагаан идээ, боов, бууз, ааруул; grammar: comitative -тай for 'with/having' food (сүүтэй цай, махтай бууз) vs. reflexive -аа; EN: ordinals for layers of ul boov (1st, 2nd, 3rd), 'on the table', 'in the bowl'

Planning the three days of visiting; vocabulary: нэг дэх өдөр, хоёр дахь өдөр, айлаар явах, бэлэг, мөнгөн дэвсгэрт, баяр хүргэе; grammar: combining comitative and reflexive (эхнэртэйгээ, хүүхдүүдтэйгээ очно); EN: ordinals 21st-31st, dates with 'on the 1st of February', 'in February'

Telling a friend about your holiday and comparing customs; vocabulary: уламжлал, баяр, шинэ жил, хүлээн авах, зочилсон, ойр дотнын хүмүүс; grammar: review of -аа/-ээ and -тай/-тэй in short narratives with past -сан/-лаа; EN: dates with in/on/at (in winter, on the 15th of February, at midnight), ordinals review

units.scope: professions, workplace; agent suffix -ч, юу хийдэг вэ; EN: What do you do?, a/an with jobs

lessons.focus: Meeting someone at a party and asking about their job; core professions (teacher, doctor, driver, student, nurse, engineer); Та юу хийдэг вэ? / Би ... байна, and English What do you do? / I'm a ...

Naming professions by what people do; agent suffix -ч with vowel harmony (жолооч, тогооч, хөгжимчин, уран бүтээлч, худалдагч); English a/an before consonant and vowel sounds with jobs (a cook, an engineer)
Describing where people work; workplace vocabulary (office, hospital, school, shop, factory, restaurant); locative -д and -т ажилладаг, and English He works at/in ..., She works for ...

lessons.title_mn: Танай гэр бүлийнхэн юу хийдэг вэ?
lessons.focus: Talking about family members' jobs in a family photo chat; family plus job vocabulary (farmer, herder, lawyer, accountant, businessman); third-person юу хийдэг вэ? / ... байна/ажилладаг; English What does he/she do? with a/an and third-person -s

Describing job duties and daily tasks of a colleague or friend; work verbs (teach, treat, drive, cook, write, sell, help); habitual -даг/-дэг/-дог/-дөг with objects, and English present simple for job duties (A nurse helps patients)

Chatting with a friend about the job you have, used to want, or would like; review of professions and workplaces; combining -ч nouns, ажилладаг, and дуртай/хүсч байна in short answers; English I want to be a/an ..., I work as a ...

units.scope: phone calls, texts, invitations; voluntative -ъя/-ая/-ье, -цгаая; EN: let's, Would you like...?

lessons.title_mn: Сайн байна уу, хэн залгаж байна вэ?
lessons.focus: Answering and starting a phone call; phone vocabulary (утас, дугаар, залгах, хариулах, сонсогдохгүй байна); Mongolian: уулзъя/залгая-style intro with 'Байна уу?', 'Би ... байна'; EN: 'Hello, this is... Can I speak to...?'
Suggesting something to a friend; places and activities (кино үзэх, кофе уух, алхах, цай уух); voluntative -ъя/-ая/-ье/-я (явъя, уулзъя, хийе, идье); EN: Let's + verb, 'Let's go to the park'

Inviting a group and making plans with friends; group outings (пикник, наадам үзэх, хамт найзууд); plural voluntative -цгаая/-цгээе/-цгоое/-цгөөе; EN: Let's + verb for groups, 'Shall we...?', 'How about...?'

Polite invitations to dinner, a birthday or Tsagaan Sar visit; invitation vocabulary (урих, зочин, төрсөн өдөр, найр); 'Ирэх үү?', 'Манайд зочилоорой', 'Ирэхгүй юу?'; EN: Would you like to...? Would you like some...? I'd love to.

Accepting, declining politely and suggesting another time; phrases (болно, баяртай байна, уучлаарай, завгүй байна, өөр өдөр); combine voluntative with reasons ('Одоо завгүй байна, маргааш уулзъя'); EN: I'd love to, I'm afraid I can't, How about...?

Writing short texts and invitations by phone; messaging vocabulary (мессеж, хариу бичих, цаг, хаяг, ирэх үү?), informal abbreviations and emoji; review of voluntative, -цгаая and invitations; EN: short texts, 'See you at 6!', 'Let's meet at...', 'Would you like to...?'

units.scope: appointments, sequences of actions; converbs -ж/-ч and -аад/-ээд; EN: before/after + -ing, present continuous for future

lessons.focus: Making and confirming appointments with a dentist, a teacher or a friend; vocabulary: appointment, meeting, schedule, today/tomorrow/next week, time of day; grammar: present continuous for fixed future plans (I'm meeting Bold at 3), with Mongolian -на/-нэ and цагтай уулзана

Chatting with a friend about weekend and next-week plans; vocabulary: common activities (visit, shop, study, meet, travel), time phrases (this evening, on Saturday, next month); grammar: asking and answering about plans in present continuous (What are you doing...? I'm not working on Sunday), with Mongolian future -на and яах вэ/юу хийх вэ

Describing a simple sequence of actions in a morning routine; vocabulary: first, then, next, finally, wake up, wash, dress, eat breakfast; grammar: Mongolian converb -аад/-ээд/-оод/-өөд for completed actions in sequence (босоод хоол идэв), with EN sequence words first/then/after that

Talking about how and while doing things at home and on the way to work; vocabulary: listen to music, walk, drink tea, read, travel by bus; grammar: Mongolian converb -ж/-ч (чихэж/сонсож яваад, цай уугаад) for simultaneous or linked actions and in -ж байна chains; EN: while + -ing as a contrast

Ordering events in a daily schedule at work or university; vocabulary: before, after, lecture, lunch, finish, homework, go home; grammar: EN before/after + -ing (After eating, I call my mother); Mongolian -аад/-ээд дараа, -хын өмнө/-сны дараа

Review: telling a partner or writing a full weekly plan with appointments and sequences (visit the doctor, then meet friends, after that go to the countryside); vocabulary: plan, free, busy, reschedule, can't make it; grammar: combining present continuous for future, before/after + -ing, and Mongolian converbs -ж/-ч and -аад/-ээд in connected text

units.scope: ordering khuushuur, cafés, paying; -мaар байна, optative -аасай/-ээсэй; EN: I'd like, Could I...?

lessons.focus: Arriving at a restaurant or café; vocabulary: table, menu, waiter, free seat, how many people; grammar: Мониторинг байна уу? 'Ширээ байна уу?', 'Хоёр хүн' counting people, EN: A table for two, please / Do you have a table?

Looking at a menu in a Ulaanbaatar café; vocabulary: khuushuur, buuz, tsuivan, soup, salad, tea, coffee, juice, dessert; grammar: asking about dishes with юу/ямар and 'Энэ юу вэ?', EN: What is in it? / Does it have...?
Placing an order with the waiter; vocabulary: order, portion, with/without meat, spicy, drinks; grammar: wish with -маар байна (Хуушуур идмээр байна), EN: I'd like... / I'd like to have...

Polite requests and small changes to an order; vocabulary: water, napkin, spoon, fork, salt, more, another; grammar: optative -аасай/-ээсэй (Ус авчирсан бол сайн, Нэмж өгөөсэй), EN: Could I have...? / Could I get...?

Talking about taste and small problems; vocabulary: delicious, salty, hot, cold, fresh, too much, wrong order; grammar: combining -маар байна and -аасай to express wishes politely, EN: I'd like it hotter / Could you bring it again?

Paying, splitting the bill and tipping; vocabulary: bill, card, cash, change, receipt, tip, tögrög amounts; grammar: review of -маар байна and -аасай/-ээсэй in payment requests (Тооцоогоо хиймээр байна), EN: Could I have the bill? / Can we pay separately?

units.scope: landscapes, five types of livestock; superlative хамгийн; EN: superlatives, the with geographic names

lessons.focus: Looking at a landscape photo from Mongolia; vocabulary: уул, гол, нуур, тал, говь, ой, хээр, далай; EN: geographic nouns with and without the (the Altai Mountains, Lake Khuvsgul, the Gobi Desert)

Visiting a herder family in the countryside; vocabulary: адуу, үхэр, тэмээ, хонь, ямаа, uri and cub names (морь, ботго, хураага); EN: plural nouns of animals (sheep, goats, horses) and a lot of / some for counting herds
Comparing animals and places in a quiz game; vocabulary: том, жижиг, урт, өндөр, хурдан, удаан, хүнд; MN: хамгийн + adjective; EN: superlatives with -est and the (the tallest, the fastest)

lessons.title_en: The Longest River, the Highest Mountain
lessons.title_mn: Хамгийн урт гол, хамгийн өндөр уул
lessons.focus: Talking about Mongolia's and the world's geography facts; vocabulary: Сэлэнгэ мөрөн, Хөвсгөл нуур, Хүйтэн оргил, Говь, Монгол Алтай; MN: хамгийн with noun phrases and -аас ablative for 'of/in'; EN: the + superlative with in/of (the largest lake in Mongolia), the with rivers, seas, mountain ranges

Choosing favorites on a nature trip (animals, seasons, views); vocabulary: сайхан, үзэсгэлэнтэй, аюултай, сонирхолтой, дуртай; MN: хамгийн дуртай, хамгийн сайхан; EN: most + long adjectives, irregular good/best, bad/worst

Describing a favorite natural place and animal to a friend or in a short post; review vocabulary of landscapes and livestock; grammar review: хамгийн and superlatives, the with geographic names, building a short paragraph

units.scope: life experiences; -ж үзсэн, -ж байсан; EN: present perfect with ever/never

lessons.focus: Chatting about places visited in Mongolia and abroad (Terelj, Khuvsgul, Beijing, Seoul); travel destinations and verbs of going; Mongolian -ж байсан for having been somewhere (очиж байсан), EN: present perfect of be/go with ever/never (Have you ever been to...?, I've been to...)

Talking at a table with a foreign friend about food tried for the first time (airag, tsuivan, sushi, spicy dishes); food and taste adjectives; Mongolian -ж үзсэн (идэж үзсэн, уугаад үзсэн) for trying experiences, EN: present perfect with ever in questions (Have you ever tried...?) and past participles eaten/drunk/tried

Admitting things you have never done (ride a camel, fly in a plane, see snow in the desert); first-time experiences and adventure activities; negation with -ж үзээгүй and хэзээ ч ... үгүй, EN: never with present perfect and have/haven't + past participle, short answers (Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.)

Talking about skills and experiences at school and work (learned to swim, drove a car, worked at a shop, studied English); learning and work vocabulary; contrast -ж байсан (state or experience in the past) vs -ж үзсэн (tried), EN: irregular past participles (done, seen, written, taken, driven, met)

lessons.title_mn: Нэг удаа, хоёр удаа, олон удаа
lessons.focus: Telling how often and how recently you did things, e.g. a friend asking about films, concerts or wrestling matches seen; frequency words and counting times; нэг удаа, хоёр удаа, хэд хэдэн удаа, саяхан, EN: ever/never/already/yet/just, once/twice/three times, been vs gone

Interviewing a classmate for a school project and reporting results (travel, food, sports, skills), then follow-up questions about when and where; review vocabulary of life experiences; combining -ж үзсэн/-ж байсан with -сан/-лаа for details, EN: switching from present perfect to past simple (Have you been to Japan? When did you go?)

units.scope: classes, exams, dorms; conditional -вал/-вэл/-бал/-бэл; EN: first conditional, unless

lessons.focus: Registering for courses at the university office; faculties, majors, credits, timetable vocabulary (мэргэжил, хичээл, багш, хуваарь); simple real conditions with -вал/-вэл/-бал/-бэл (e.g. Хэрэв хичээл эрт эхэлбэл...) and English first conditional form: if + present simple, will + verb

Planning study time with classmates in the library; exam and study vocabulary (шалгалт, лекц, дэвтэр, давтах, тэмдэглэл); consequences and results with -вал/-вэл (Давтвал, сайн оноо авна) and English if-clauses with will/won't, including 'if' at the start or middle of a sentence

Sharing a room, house rules and roommates in a dorm; dorm and daily-life vocabulary (байр, өрөөний хамаатан, цэвэрлэгээ, чимээ шуугиан, түлхүүр); conditions with requests and warnings using -вал/-вэл + imperative/-на, and English first conditional with imperatives (If you go out, lock the door)

Talking about grades, retakes and what happens if you fail; grade and result vocabulary (оноо, дүн, тэнцэх, унах, дахин өгөх); negative conditions with -хгүй бол, -вал + гүй, and English 'unless' meaning 'if not' (Unless you study, you won't pass)

Discussing applying for scholarships and studying abroad with an adviser; application vocabulary (тэтгэлэг, өргөдөл, элсэлт, бичиг баримт, шаардлага); chaining conditions and plans (-вал ... -х юм бол), and English first conditional with may/might/can/should and when vs if

Giving and asking for advice in a student forum post or chat; mixed campus vocabulary review (ажил хийх, цагийн ажил, дадлага, санаа зовох, амрах); review of -вал/-вэл/-бал/-бэл with all verb types and English first conditional and unless in short connected paragraphs

units.scope: wrestling, horse racing, archery; passive -гд-; EN: passive voice in present and past

lessons.focus: Introducing Naadam to a foreign friend in Ulaanbaatar; vocabulary: Naadam, the opening ceremony, Central Stadium, July 11-13, wrestling, horse racing, archery, spectators; grammar: passive voice in English present (is/are + past participle: 'Naadam is held every July') and the Mongolian passive suffix -гд- in its basic present forms (зохион байгуулагдана, болдог → болгогддог)

Watching a wrestling match with a relative; vocabulary: бөх, зодог, шуудаг, цол (аварга, арслан, заан), давах, унах, дэвэх, 9 rounds; grammar: passive in present for rules and customs ('The winner is called an arslan', '...гэж нэрлэгддэг') with Mongolian -гд- verbs like нэрлэгдэх, мэдэгдэх, шалгагдах

Describing the race on the steppe; vocabulary: уралдаан, хүүхэд уяач, уяач, соёолон, шүдлэн, хязааланд ... ; айрагдах, 'Giingoo' song, finish line, the winners' praise; grammar: English passive in simple present with by-agent ('The horses are trained by herders', 'The song is sung before the race') and Mongolian -гд- with agent expressed by -аас/-ээс

Visiting the archery field and talking about equipment and traditions; vocabulary: нум, сум, суры, харвагч, шагай, онох, алдах, зорилт, team; grammar: English passive with modal and negative/question forms ('Arrows are not shot from..., Is the target hit?') and Mongolian -гд- negatives and questions (онуулаагүй, харвагдахгүй)

Telling a friend about results and events of last year's Naadam; vocabulary: ялагч, түрүүлэх, шалгаруулах, медаль, шагнал, rank, record; grammar: English passive in past simple ('The winner was awarded a title', 'Three records were broken') and Mongolian past passive -гдсан/-гдлаа/-гдав (шагнагдсан, зарлагдсан, шалгарсан)

Comparing old and modern Naadam in a short article or museum talk; vocabulary: уламжлал, өв, ЮНЕСКО, хадгалагдах, өөрчлөгдөх, зохион байгуулах, local naadam in sums; grammar: review and contrast of present vs past passive in English ('was held in the past, is held today') and in Mongolian (-гдсан vs -гддаг), plus when to use active vs passive

units.scope: narrating past events; converbs -хад/-хэд, -тал/-тэл, -саар/-сээр; EN: past continuous, when/while

lessons.focus: Opening a story and setting the scene; story-words (нэгэн удаа, дараа нь, эцэст нь, гэнэт, тэгээд); review of past -сан/-лаа and introduction of past continuous in English (was/were + -ing) for background description

lessons.title_mn: Тэр үед юу болж байсан бэ?
lessons.focus: Describing a scene in the countryside or at home at a given moment; everyday activities and background details; Mongolian -ж/-ч байсан for ongoing past action vs. simple past; English past continuous statements and questions (was cooking, were sleeping)

Telling what happened at the moment of another event (a phone call, a knock at the ger door, arriving at a station); interrupted actions; converb -хад/-хэд ('when/upon ...ing'): Би гэрт ороход ээж чай чанаж байсан; English when + past simple with past continuous

A long wait or a surprise turn in a story (waiting for a bus in winter, searching for a lost horse); time expressions and surprise (гэнэт, санамсаргүй); converb -тал/-тэл ('until / while suddenly'); English while and until with past continuous and past simple

Quick chains of events on a trip or at a celebration (arriving at Naadam, getting home after a long day); sequence and immediate result; converb -саар/-сээр ('as soon as / while continually doing'); English as soon as, while, and two simultaneous past continuous actions

Telling a complete personal story (an adventure on a trip, a funny mishap, a memorable family event) aloud and in writing; mixing -хад/-хэд, -тал/-тэл, -саар/-сээр with past tenses and story-linking words; English narrative combining past simple, past continuous, when and while

units.scope: agreeing and disagreeing; quotative гэж, гэж бодож байна; EN: I think that, I agree/disagree, so/because

lessons.title_mn: Та юу гэж бодож байна вэ?
lessons.focus: Friends chat about a new café in Ulaanbaatar and ask for each other's views; basic opinion words (сайн, муу, сонирхолтой, хэцүү, үнэтэй); asking and giving an opinion with 'гэж бодож байна' / 'миний бодлоор' and EN 'I think (that)...', 'What do you think?'

lessons.title_mn: Би санал нийлж байна, нийлэхгүй байна
lessons.focus: Discussing a group trip plan at work or school; agreement and disagreement phrases (тийм ээ, үнэн, санал нэг байна, санал нийлэхгүй байна, би тэгж бодохгүй байна); negative form -гүй with бодох; EN 'I agree/disagree', 'I don't think so', 'Me too', 'Exactly'
Explaining why you prefer city or countryside life; reason words (учир нь, учраас, тиймээс, ... тул, яагаад гэвэл); linking reasons with Mongolian -ж/-аад, 'учраас' and EN 'because' and 'so'

Sharing what others believe at a family dinner, such as grandparents' views on food and traditions; vocabulary of beliefs and habits (уламжлал, үзэл бодол, итгэх, үздэг); quotative гэж with хэлэх, бодох, итгэх; EN 'My grandmother thinks that...', 'People say that...'

A meeting or class discussion where views differ; softening phrases (магадгүй, жаахан өөрөөр бодож байна, гэхдээ, зарим талаараа); hedged opinions with -х юм шиг байна, байх гэж бодож байна; EN 'I see your point, but...', 'I'm not sure', 'maybe', 'in my opinion'

A group discussion about a social topic (school uniforms, phones in class, or a new park) with opinions, agreement, reasons and a decision; combining all unit structures; consolidating гэж бодох, гэж хэлэх, учир нь with EN 'I think that..., because..., so...', 'I agree/disagree'

units.scope: advice, rules, permission; -х хэрэгтэй, -х ёстой, -ж болно; EN: should, must, have to, may

lessons.focus: A friend feels tired and stressed and asks for help; health and lifestyle vocabulary (sleep, exercise, rest, water, vegetables); giving friendly advice with -х хэрэгтэй (Та илүү унтах хэрэгтэй) and EN should/shouldn't
First day at a new job or school and learning the rules; vocabulary of rules (дүрэм, цаг баримтлах, хоцрох, зөвшөөрөл, дүрэмт хувцас); stating obligation with -х ёстой and EN must / mustn't

Comparing strong necessity with mild advice in daily situations (documents, deadlines, tickets); vocabulary of duties and necessities; contrast -х ёстой vs -х хэрэгтэй and EN have to / don't have to vs must / should

Visiting a ger and asking for permission at someone's home and in public places; vocabulary of polite requests (орж болох уу, суухад болох уу, зураг авч болох уу); permission with -ж болно / -ж болох уу and EN may / can / could

Signs and prohibitions in the city, parks, and public transport, plus ger etiquette taboos; vocabulary of signs and bans (тамхи татаж болохгүй, зогсоох хориотой, хориглоно); prohibition with -ж болохгүй, -…гүй байх ёстой and EN mustn't / not allowed to / can't

Advising a foreign visitor about travel and customs in Mongolia (Naadam, ger visit, winter trip); mixed vocabulary of customs, clothing and safety; combining -х хэрэгтэй, -х ёстой, -ж болно/болохгүй in short advice texts and EN should, must, have to, may in review

units.scope: describing people and things; participles -сан/-х/-даг as modifiers; EN: relative clauses who/which/that

lessons.focus: Thanking and describing a helpful person (neighbor, teacher, friend); personality and character adjectives (kind, patient, funny, strict); past participle -сан/-сэн/-сон/-сөн as a modifier before a noun (надад тусалсан хүн) and English 'who' for people (the man who helped me)

lessons.title_en: The Things I Use Every Day
lessons.focus: Talking about favorite everyday objects and gadgets (phone, bag, kettle, notebook); household and personal items; habitual participle -даг/-дэг/-дог/-дөг as a modifier (би өдөр бүр хэрэглэдэг утас) and English 'which/that' for things (the phone that I use every day)

Arranging to meet a person you don't know yet at a station or café; appearance and clothing description (tall, wearing a deel, glasses); future participle -х/-ах/-эх/-ох/-өх as a modifier (миний уулзах хүн, бидний очих газар) and English relative clauses with 'who/that' plus will/going to

Recommending places in Ulaanbaatar and the countryside (café, market, monastery, hot spring); place and building words; combining participles with nouns for places (бидний хоол идсэн ресторан, хүмүүс очдог газар) and English 'where' and 'that' in relative clauses (the café where we met)

Describing a friend's relatives, work, and where they live in a longer description; relationship and occupation vocabulary; participles with possessives and cases (аав нь ажилладаг компани, ээж нь төрсөн нутаг) and English 'whose' and object-relative clauses without a pronoun (the woman I met)

lessons.title_mn: Хэн бэ, юу вэ гэж таа
lessons.focus: Playing a guessing game and writing a short portrait of a person or object; mixed vocabulary review for people, things, and places; choosing between -сан, -даг, and -х participles in one description, with negation (хэзээ ч уншаагүй ном), and English relative clauses (who/which/that/where/whose) with defining details

units.scope: air pollution, traffic, ger districts; causative -уул/-үүл, -лга; EN: too/enough, much/many/a lot of

lessons.focus: Talking about air pollution in Ulaanbaatar in winter; vocabulary: утаа, агаар, шүүгч, амьсгалах, coal stove, mask, health effects; grammar: describing the problem with 'a lot of / much / many' (их утаа, олон машин) vs. EN much (uncountable) / many (countable) / a lot of in statements, questions and negatives

Complaining about rush-hour traffic and commuting; vocabulary: түгжрэл, гэрлэн дохио, зам, замын түгжрэл, автобус, жолооч, хоцрох; grammar: EN too + adjective/too much/too many (too crowded, too many cars) and MN хэт/хэтэрхий + adjective, -сан учраас for reasons

Describing everyday conditions in a ger district; vocabulary: гэр хороолол, түлш, нүүрс, ус, цахилгаан, ариун цэврийн байгууламж, хашаа; grammar: EN adjective + enough / enough + noun (warm enough, enough water) and MN хангалттай, -х хэмжээний, with negation -гүй

Talking about what makes problems happen or stop; vocabulary: утаа ихэсгэх, багасгах, хориглох, шилжүүлэх, цэвэрлэх, сайжруулах; grammar: causative -уул/-үүл (-лга) in simple sentences: ажиллуулах, ойлгуулах, нүүлгэх, with EN make/let/have someone do for comparison

Reading and discussing news about city solutions; vocabulary: цахилгаан шугам, шатахуун, шинэ шугам, метро, цэвэр түлш, барилга, захиргаа; grammar: causative in news-style sentences (нүүлгэв, суулгуулав, барьж байгуулуулах) and nominal -лга (хяналт, тээвэрлэлт, халаалт), plus mixed too/enough/much/many review

lessons.title_en: Our Ideas for a Better City
lessons.focus: Giving short proposals and writing a letter to the district office; vocabulary: санал, гомдол, сайжруулах, оролцох, нийтийн тээвэр, ногоон байгууламж; grammar: combining causatives, too/enough and much/many/a lot of to explain problems and suggest solutions in a short paragraph

units.scope: passing on messages and news; гэсэн, гэж хэлсэн, гэнэ; EN: reported speech, say vs tell

lessons.focus: Relaying a simple message from a friend or family member; verbs of speaking (хэлэх, асуух, хариулах, мэдэгдэх); direct vs. indirect speech with гэж хэлсэн, and EN: reported statements with said (that) and the present-to-past shift (I am coming → he said he was coming)

Passing on instructions and messages at home and work, such as a mother's note or a boss's message; message vocabulary (захиа, зөвлөгөө, захиалга, мэдээ); EN: say vs. tell (tell someone, say to someone), reported past with backshift (we were, he had); MN: хэн нэгэнд хэлэх with dative and the choice between хэлэх, ярих, дуудах

Telling a colleague what a teacher, doctor, or clerk asked or requested; question words and request verbs (асуух, хүсэх, захих, санал болгох); MN: -х гэж асуусан, -х уу гэж асуусан, -аач гэж хэлсэн, and EN: reported questions with ask if/whether and wh- words in statement order; tell someone to do

Sharing hearsay and rumors among neighbors and friends, such as news from the countryside or ger district; vocabulary of news and rumor (цуу яриа, сурагтай, мэдээ дуулах, эх сурвалж); MN: sentence-final гэнэ and гэсэн as a reported or hearsay marker (ирнэ гэнэ, орсон гэнэ); EN: they say, apparently, I heard that, reportedly, reporting verbs (claim, mention, explain)

lessons.title_en: The Message Left on the Phone
lessons.focus: Listening to voicemails and texts and summarizing them for someone else; vocabulary of voicemail, deadlines, and meetings (үлдээх, дамжуулах, дахин залгах, уулзалт цуцлах); MN: noun-modifying гэсэн (ирнэ гэсэн захиа), -сан гэж хэлсэн and time shift; EN: reported time and place changes (today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there)

Summarizing a news story or a conversation with several speakers, such as a weather report, a Naadam announcement, or a family discussion; news and announcement vocabulary (мэдэгдэл, зарлах, мэдээлэх, тайлбарлах, амлах); MN: combining гэж хэлсэн, гэсэн, and гэнэ in a short summary; EN: reporting verbs (announce, promise, warn, suggest, explain) with that/to-infinitive/-ing patterns

units.scope: internet, social media, news; concessive -сан ч, гэхдээ; EN: although, used to

lessons.focus: Home and café Wi-Fi, phones and laptops; devices and internet vocabulary (утас, зөөврийн компьютер, wifi, нууц үг, холбогдох, татах); review of -ж байна and -даг habits, plus EN: present simple for how often we go online

Talking with a grandparent or parent about how things used to be; old and new technology (захидал, лангуу, дугаар шивэх, мессеж); EN: used to + verb for past habits, with contrast to the present using -даг байсан / одоо

Chatting about Facebook, Instagram and TikTok among friends; social media vocabulary (пост, дагагч, лайк, сэтгэгдэл, чат, профайл); EN: used to vs. present simple, negatives and questions (didn't use to, Did you use to...?) in a social-media context

Following the news on websites, TV and apps; news vocabulary (мэдээ, гарчиг, сурвалжлага, эх сурвалж, худал мэдээ, найдвартай); EN: although + clause in sentences about news, with the Mongolian concessive -сан ч / -даг ч introduced for the same idea

Discussing pros and cons of technology with a colleague; online shopping, privacy, screen time; MN: гэхдээ, -сан ч, -х ч юм бол, and ч гэсэн for contrast; EN: although/though/but compared, sentence-initial vs. mid-sentence although with commas

lessons.title_en: Then and Now: Tech in My Life
lessons.title_mn: Өмнө ба одоо: технологи миний амьдралд
lessons.focus: Writing a short blog post or voice message about how technology has changed daily life in Ulaanbaatar and the countryside; mixed review of tech vocabulary; combining used to with although and -сан ч / гэхдээ in a connected paragraph

units.scope: CVs, interviews, polite formal speech; honorific verbs, formal та forms; EN: formal requests, would/could

lessons.focus: Finding a vacancy in a job ad and understanding its requirements; vocabulary: vacancy, position, requirements, experience, salary, deadline (сул орон тоо, албан тушаал, шаардлага, туршлага, цалин, хугацаа); grammar: formal written requirement phrases with -х шаардлагатай, -сан байх; EN: formal noun phrases in ads and 'applicants must have/be able to'

Preparing a CV and cover letter; vocabulary: education, skills, work history, references, strengths (боловсрол, ур чадвар, ажлын туршлага, зөвлөмж, давуу тал); grammar: concise past and perfective forms for achievements (-сан, -в, -аад төгссөн); EN: past simple vs present perfect in CVs, action verbs (managed, developed, organized)

Arriving at the office, introducing yourself and making small talk with the panel; vocabulary: appointment, reception, panel, to introduce oneself, punctuality (цаг товлох, хүлээн авах, комисс, өөрийгөө танилцуулах); grammar: formal та forms and honorific greetings (сайн байна уу, танилцахад таатай байна, хүлээж байсан); EN: polite openings, 'It's a pleasure to meet you', 'Thank you for seeing me'

Talking about your strengths, weaknesses, experience and motivation; vocabulary: strength, weakness, achievement, teamwork, responsibility, motivation (давуу тал, сул тал, амжилт, багаар ажиллах, хариуцлага, урам зориг); grammar: honorific verb forms for respected persons and the speaker's humble forms (эрхэм, захирал танд, -т бий, хэлэх, айлтгах, сонсоно уу); EN: would/could for hedged self-description, 'I would say that...', 'I could manage...'

Asking the employer about salary, schedule and duties, and requesting clarification; vocabulary: working hours, contract, probation, benefits, leave, training (ажлын цаг, гэрээ, туршилтын хугацаа, нэмэгдэл урамшуулал, амралт, сургалт); grammar: polite request forms -на уу, -ж болох уу, -вал зүгээр юм, -уулах; EN: formal requests with would/could: 'Could you tell me...?', 'Would it be possible to...?', 'I was wondering if...'

Thanking the interviewers, following up by email and responding to an offer or rejection; vocabulary: offer, decision, follow-up, to accept, to decline, regards (санал, шийдвэр, дахин холбогдох, зөвшөөрөх, татгалзах, хүндэтгэсэн); grammar: formal closing and gratitude forms with honorifics (баярлалаа → танд талархаж байна, хүндэтгэн, -сан явдалд); EN: formal email phrases with would/could: 'I would be grateful if...', 'We would like to offer you...', 'Could you confirm...?'

units.scope: imagined and missed situations; -сан бол, -х байсан; EN: second and third conditionals, wish

lessons.focus: Daydreaming about money and luck; money, lottery and big-purchase vocabulary (сугалаа, хожих, үл хөдлөх хөрөнгө, аялал); EN: second conditional (If I won..., I would...), MN: hypothetical -вал/-бал with -х байсан / -на for unreal present situations

Giving imaginary advice to a friend about work, housing or study choices; decision and life-choice vocabulary (шийдвэр, сонголт, нүүх, ажил солих); EN: If I were you, I would... and were with all subjects, MN: -сан бол + -х байсан for imagined advice

Regretting small everyday mishaps (missed bus, forgotten umbrella, late arrival); time, transport and mishap vocabulary (хоцрох, алдах, март-); EN: third conditional (If I had known, I would have...), MN: -сан бол ... -х байсан for past unreal

Talking about missed opportunities in study, career and travel; opportunity and consequence vocabulary (боломж, харамсах, үр дүн, тэтгэлэг); EN: mixed conditionals and could have / might have / should have, MN: -х байсан with modal nuances and үр дагавар clauses

Expressing wishes and regrets about present and past (wish I had more time, wish I'd studied); feelings and regret vocabulary (харамсал, мөрөөдөл, хүсэл); EN: wish + past simple / past perfect, if only, MN: -сан бол гэж хүсэх, -аасай, -сан бол сайн байсан юм

Discussing how life, a country or a family story might have been different (e.g. if Mongolia had not..., if my grandparents had stayed in the countryside); history, family and cause-effect vocabulary; EN: reviewing all conditionals, wish and as if / suppose, MN: combined -сан бол / -х байсан in extended storytelling

units.scope: Chinggis Khaan, nomadic heritage; past -в, evidential -жээ/-чээ; EN: past perfect, narrative tenses

lessons.focus: reading a short museum panel about Chinggis Khaan's life; vocabulary: хаан, эзэнт гүрэн, нэгтгэх, төрөх, залгамжлах, ish dates and centuries; grammar: formal narrative past -в (төрөв, нэгтгэв) vs. everyday -сан/-лаа; EN: past simple for biography contrasted with simple dates

lessons.title_en: Life on the Steppe: Nomadic Heritage
lessons.focus: a guide explaining how nomads lived at a heritage camp; vocabulary: нүүдэл, бэлчээр, хошуу мал, гэр, уламжлал, зуншлага/өвөлжөө; grammar: describing past habits and states with -даг байсан and -ж байв; EN: past continuous and used to in descriptions of historical life

archaeologists and visitors react to a newly found artifact; vocabulary: малтлага, олдвор, булш, хөшөө, эртний, судлаач; grammar: evidential/mirative -жээ/-чээ for newly discovered or inferred facts; EN: reporting discoveries with apparently, it turns out, must have been

lessons.title_en: Before the Empire: Events in Order
lessons.focus: explaining which events happened before others in the rise of the Mongol Empire; vocabulary: удирдагч, овог аймаг, дайн, холбоо, байлдан дагуулал, хуучин/шинэ; grammar: sequencing with -сан байв, -аас өмнө/хойно, -аад; EN: past perfect (had + past participle) vs past simple

retelling a legend such as the Secret History of the Mongols to a group; vocabulary: domestic and heroic story words: домог, уламжлал, баатар, нууц товчоо, өв залгамжлал, үлгэр; grammar: mixing -в, -лаа, -жээ, and -сан байна to shape a narrative; EN: narrative tenses (past simple, past continuous, past perfect) in one story with linking words

a short talk or discussion at a cultural center about preserving heritage sites and traditions (UNESCO, Naadam, throat singing); vocabulary: хамгаалах, өв, ЮНЕСКО, дурсгал, үеийн үед, сэргээх; grammar: review of -в, -жээ/-чээ and past forms in an informative summary; EN: review of narrative tenses and past perfect in a short presentation

units.scope: jobs market, mining, prices; nominalizations -лт/-лт, -л; EN: noun phrases, collocations

lessons.focus: reading a short economic overview; GDP, growth, export, import, budget, sector; introducing verbal nouns with -лт/-лт (өсөлт, бууралт, хөгжил) and the EN noun phrase pattern adjective + noun (economic growth, foreign trade)

visiting Oyu Tolgoi or Erdenet and talking to a worker; coal, copper, gold, deposit, extraction, license; nominalizing actions with -лт (олборлолт, боловсруулалт, тээвэрлэлт) and EN noun + noun compounds (copper mine, mining license, safety regulations)

discussing unemployment and hiring on a news show; vacancy, salary, employer, skills, unemployment rate; -л nominalizations (ажил, нийлүүлэлт contrasted with -лт, засвар, хэрэгцээ) and EN collocations with job/work (apply for, create jobs, labor shortage, full-time position)

family and shop talk about rising prices of meat, fuel and rent; inflation, exchange rate, wage, cost of living; nominalizations as subjects (үнийн өсөлт, цалингийн нэмэгдэлт) with genitive chains and EN collocations (prices rise/soar, cut costs, living standards)

listening to a business forum on foreign investment, exports to China, and infrastructure; investor, tax, contract, revenue, loan; compounds like хөрөнгө оруулалт, бүтээн байгуулалт, хэлэлцээр and long EN noun phrases (foreign direct investment, a long-term trade agreement) with pre- and post-modification

summarizing figures and trends in a short report about mining and the economy; increase, decline, share, forecast; combining -лт/-л nominalizations in formal sentences (экспортын өсөлт нь ... хүргэв) and EN data-description collocations (a sharp rise in, account for, be projected to)

units.scope: education, migration, youth; хэдийгээр ... ч, connectors; EN: discourse markers, emphasis structures

lessons.focus: Students sign up for a university debating society and learn the rules of a debate; debate vocabulary (мэтгэлцээ, аргумент, санал, эсэргүүцэх, дэмжих, шүүгч); English discourse markers for opening and structuring a point (firstly, to begin with, in addition, finally) and Mongolian equivalents (юуны өмнө, нэгдүгээрт, түүнчлэн, эцэст нь)

lessons.title_en: Education: Village School or City School?
lessons.title_mn: Боловсрол: хөдөөгийн сургууль уу, хотын сургууль уу?
lessons.focus: Debate on the quality and access of education in the countryside versus Ulaanbaatar; education vocabulary (боловсрол, чанар, багш нар, тэтгэлэг, дотуур байр, онлайн сургалт); хэдийгээр ... ч for concession in Mongolian; English although/even though/despite and contrast markers (however, on the other hand, nevertheless)

lessons.title_en: Moving to the City, Moving Abroad
lessons.title_mn: Хот руу, гадаад руу нүүх нь
lessons.focus: Discussion of internal migration to ger districts and emigration for study and work; migration vocabulary (нүүдэл, цагаачлал, ажил хайх, амьжиргаа, гэр бүлээсээ хол байх, буцаж ирэх); cause and result connectors in Mongolian (учраас, тиймээс, улмаар, түүнээс болж); English therefore, as a result, consequently, due to

Panel talk on youth: jobs, social media, volunteering, and generation gaps; youth vocabulary (залуучууд, өөдрөг үзэл, сайн дурын ажил, ирээдүй, хариуцлага, хөдөлмөр эрхлэлт); Mongolian listing and adding connectors (түүнээс гадна, мөн, харин, бүр) and conceding with ч ... гэсэн; English adding and contrasting markers (moreover, whereas, while, in fact)

Practicing persuasive speaking in a debate round with emphasis; emphasis vocabulary and fixed phrases (үнэхээр, ялангуяа, яг, зөвхөн, огт, чухамдаа); Mongolian emphatic particles (-ч, -ийн, бол, ш дээ) and English cleft sentences (What I mean is..., It is education that..., The reason why...) and inversion (Never have I...)

Full debate on a motion such as 'Young people should study abroad', with rebuttal and closing statements; summing up and rebutting vocabulary (няцаах, дүгнэх, нотлох баримт, зөвшилцөх, эсрэг тал, шийдвэр); combining хэдийгээр ... ч, causal and contrast connectors; English concluding and rebuttal markers (in conclusion, all things considered, that said, I would argue that)

units.scope: common proverbs and set phrases; figurative meanings; EN: idioms, phrasal verbs

lessons.focus: A grandmother shares a saying with her grandchild in a ger; what a proverb (зүйр цэцэн үг) is and how Mongolians use them; the structure of short rhyming and parallel proverbs, e.g. 'Эхнийх нь эрдэнэ' style pairs; EN: introducing a proverb ('As the saying goes', 'They say that...') and literal vs. figurative meaning

Chatting at a countryside family gathering; proverbs and idioms built on the five livestock and wild animals (морь, ямаа, чоно, бөхөн etc.); the conditional/habitual in proverbs (-вал, -даг, -сан) and the general-truth present; EN: animal idioms (a black sheep, let the cat out of the bag, a wolf in sheep's clothing) and similes with as...as

Two colleagues talk about stress and feelings at the office; set phrases with body parts (сэтгэл, зүрх, толгой, гар, нүд, чих), e.g. 'нүд тайлах', 'чих тавих'; fixed noun + verb collocations and idiomatic case use; EN: body idioms (keep an eye on, cold feet, lend a hand) and their meanings

lessons.title_mn: Ажил, мөнгө, google We хувь заяа
lessons.focus: Friends discuss a risky business decision over tea; proverbs and idioms about effort, patience, money and fortune; contrast and cause in proverbs (-ваас, -хаас өөр, ч ... ч); EN: money and work idioms (break the bank, call it a day, hit the nail on the head) and when they sound natural

A student and a flatmate sort out plans and a mishap in Ulaanbaatar; Mongolian compound and light-verb phrases (болгох, хийх, өгөх, орхих, авах as aspect/direction markers, e.g. 'бичиж өгөх', 'хийгээд орхих'); EN: phrasal verbs (give up, figure out, look into, put off, run out of), separable vs. inseparable

Giving advice and a short speech at a family celebration; choosing the right proverb or idiom for the situation, register, and avoiding overuse or clichés; softening and ironic use, adapting proverbs ('Хэлэхэд амархан...'); EN: comparing equivalent proverbs across languages and using idioms appropriately in speech and writing

units.scope: emails, applications, short essays; written register; EN: formal style, articles review

lessons.title_en: Formal or Informal? Choosing a Register
lessons.title_mn: Албан ёсны уу, чөлөөтэй юу? Хэв маягаа сонгох
lessons.focus: Comparing a text message to a friend with a formal message to a professor or office; register vocabulary (хүндэтгэсэн, мэндчилгээ, хандах, товч); written Mongolian forms (-на уу → -на уу гэж хүсье, -ж байна → -ж байгаа, formal та forms, avoiding colloquial shortenings) and EN: contractions vs full forms, formal vs informal word choice (ask for vs request, get vs receive)

Writing an email to a company or university official; email parts (субъект, мэндчилгээ, хавсралт, талархал, хүндэтгэсэн); Mongolian openers and closers (Эрхэм ...,  Хүндэтгэсэн, ... гэж хүсье) with polite request endings -уулахыг хүсье / -ж өгнө үү; EN: formal openings and closings (Dear Ms..., I am writing to..., Yours sincerely), polite requests with I would be grateful if

lessons.title_en: Applying for a Program or Job
lessons.focus: Writing a cover letter and application for a scholarship or job; vocabulary of applications (өргөдөл, ажлын туршлага, ур чадвар, сонирхол, зорилго); Mongolian written sentence chains with converbs and purpose -х зорилгоор, -х санаатай, nominal endings in résumé style; EN: describing experience with present perfect and past simple, and purpose clauses (to + verb, in order to)

Writing a clear 4-paragraph essay on a topic like technology or city life; essay vocabulary (оршил, гол хэсэг, дүгнэлт, нэг талаас, нөгөө талаас, жишээлбэл); Mongolian written connectors (үүнээс гадна, иймд, тиймээс, харин) and thesis sentences; EN: paragraph structure, linking words (firstly, moreover, however, therefore, in conclusion)

lessons.title_en: Making Your Writing Formal and Precise
lessons.focus: Editing a rough draft into a polished text; formal vocabulary and nominalizations (хөгжүүлэлт, хэрэгжилт, шийдвэрлэх, дүгнэх); Mongolian passive and impersonal written style (-гдах, -л байна, тусгах, анхаарах), avoiding repetition and colloquial fillers; EN: formal style (passive, nominalization, avoiding phrasal verbs and contractions, hedging with may/tend to)

lessons.title_en: Articles Review and Final Writing Task
lessons.title_mn: Тусгай нэрийн болон тодорхойлогчийн давтлага, эцсийн бичгийн даалгавар
lessons.focus: Proofreading a complete formal letter and essay for the course finale; mixed review vocabulary from the unit; Mongolian proofreading points (case endings, vowel harmony, ө/ү spelling, punctuation) and EN: articles review (a/an, the, zero article with general nouns, countable vs uncountable, geographic and institutional names)

units.title_mn: Эрүүл мэнд ба сайн сайхан амьдрал
units.scope: hospitals, insurance, stress, healthy habits; probability -х магадлалтай, -ж магадгүй; EN: must/might/can't have + past participle

lessons.focus: Registering at a hospital or clinic in Ulaanbaatar and describing symptoms to staff; vocabulary: hospital departments, referral, appointment, test, results, waiting room; grammar: review of progressive and polite requests, then the first modal of probability, -ж магадгүй (it may be that...), paired with EN: might / may for present possibility

Sorting out health insurance at a state hospital or private clinic; vocabulary: insurance card, coverage, premium, claim, reimbursement, private vs. state care; grammar: -х магадлалтай (it is likely that...) for expected outcomes; EN: must be / can't be for deductions about the present (That must be the wrong form)

Talking with a colleague or friend about work and exam stress; vocabulary: stress, anxiety, burnout, overwork, sleep problems, deadline, pressure; grammar: combining -сан + магадлалтай and -сан байж магадгүй for past probability; EN: must have / might have / can't have + past participle (She must have been exhausted)

Comparing traditional Mongolian diet and modern lifestyle, giving a health talk at a university or workplace; vocabulary: balanced diet, exercise, sleep, vitamins, fermented foods like airag, salt and sugar, walking; grammar: contrasting degrees of certainty (магадгүй, тодорхой, баттай) with -х магадлалтай; EN: can't have / couldn't have vs. might have for ruling out and allowing past explanations

Supporting a friend who seems low, and talking about counselling, rest, and asking for help; vocabulary: mood, loneliness, counsellor, support, coping, relaxation, burden; grammar: hedged, tactful speculation about feelings and reasons with -ж магадгүй, -сан бололтой; EN: must/might/may have + past participle in sensitive conversation (You might have been feeling overwhelmed)

Playing doctor and patient in a case-study role-play: a doctor and a patient reason about symptoms, causes, and test results; vocabulary: diagnosis, cause, risk factor, recovery, prevention, follow-up visit, lab results; grammar: consolidation of -х магадлалтай, -ж магадгүй, -сан байж магадгүй for present and past inference; EN: full contrast of must/might/may/could/can't + have + past participle

units.scope: dzud, desertification, herders' lives; purpose -хын тулд, -х тусам; EN: the more... the more, so that / in order to

lessons.focus: Explaining the dzud to a foreign friend; dzud types (white, black, iron), snow, frost, livestock loss, pasture (зуд, цас, хүйтэн, мал, бэлчээр, хужир); review of descriptive past and evidential -жээ/-чээ for reporting what happened in a bad winter; EN: narrative past tenses to describe a disaster

A herder family describes the seasonal migration cycle and daily work; vocabulary: нүүдэл, өвөлжөө, хаваржаа, хадлан, сүү, ноос; purpose -хын тулд for stating why they do things; EN: in order to / to + verb

Planning how to protect animals before the cold; vocabulary: өвс, тэжээл, хашаа, хороо, бэлтгэх, нөөцлөх, даатгал; -хын тулд with concrete plans and goals; EN: so that + clause (so that the animals survive) vs in order to + verb

Talking with a scientist about desertification, drought and drying rivers; vocabulary: цөлжилт, ган, уур амьсгал, дулаарал, гол горхи, ширгэх, хуурайшилт; nominal descriptions of causes and effects using -лт and -х; EN: cause and effect vocabulary, present perfect for change (has become drier)

Discussing trends such as heat, overgrazing and migration to Ulaanbaatar; vocabulary: нэмэгдэх, буурах, өсөх, хэт бэлчээрлэлт, хүн амын шилжилт; -х тусам for proportional change; EN: the more... the more, the + comparative structures

Radio-style debate and community meeting proposing solutions such as tree planting, pasture rules and herder cooperatives; vocabulary: хамгаалах, нөхөн сэргээх, мод тарих, хоршоо, бодлого; combining -хын тулд and -х тусам in arguments and proposals; EN: combining in order to, so that and the more... the more in persuasive speech

units.scope: renting, work contracts, consumer rights; formal -хыг хориглоно, -сан тохиолдолд; EN: modal passives, it is said/believed that

lessons.focus: Viewing a flat in Ulaanbaatar and asking the landlord about terms; rent, deposit, utilities, tenant, landlord (түрээс, барьцаа, түрээслэгч, түрээслүүлэгч); the formal future/present -на used in written terms, plus EN: it is said/believed that for reported general claims about the rental market

Going through the clauses of a rental agreement; contract vocabulary (гэрээ, зүйл, талууд, хугацаа, дуусгавар болох); prohibitions with -хыг хориглоно and obligations in formal text; EN: modal passives (must be paid, may not be sublet, cannot be kept)

Signing a job contract and checking its terms; salary, probation, working hours, leave, notice (цалин, туршилтын хугацаа, ажлын цаг, амралт, урьдчилан мэдэгдэх); conditions with -сан тохиолдолд; EN: modal passives in contracts (will be paid, shall be given, can be terminated)

Discussing unfair dismissal, unpaid overtime and complaints to a labor office; rights, violation, compensation, dispute (эрх, зөрчил, нөхөн олговор, маргаан); combining -сан тохиолдолд with -х эрхтэй and -х үүрэгтэй; EN: it is believed/reported that, plus passive reporting of facts (is entitled to, is required to)

Returning a faulty phone or appliance and claiming a refund; warranty, receipt, refund, defect, consumer protection (баталгаа, баримт, мөнгө буцаалт, согог, хэрэглэгчийн эрх); formal notices such as -хыг хориглоно and -сан тохиолдолд in store policies; EN: modal passives in policies (can be returned within 14 days, must not be used) and it is said that

Drafting a complaint to a landlord, employer or company and requesting a remedy; complaint-letter vocabulary (гомдол, нэхэмжлэх, шийдвэрлэх, хариу хүсэх, хуулийн дагуу); review and combination of -хыг хориглоно, -сан тохиолдолд and formal requests; EN: modal passives and it is said/believed/reported that in formal writing

units.scope: morin khuur, khöömii, films, exhibitions; comparison -сан юм шиг, -сан мэт; EN: as if/as though, participle clauses

lessons.title_en: The Sound of the Morin Khuur
lessons.focus: Describing a morin khuur concert and its legend; instruments, strings, bow, melody, sound adjectives (уянгалаг, сэтгэл хөдлөм); first comparison with -сан юм шиг: 'it sounds as if a horse is galloping' (морь давхиж байгаа юм шиг сонсогдох); EN: sounds like / as if + clause

Explaining khöömii to a foreign friend at a performance; voice, breath, overtones, traditional vs modern performers; -сан мэт and -х мэт for vivid similes (уул чимээгээр хариулсан мэт); EN: as though + past/present, difference between as if, like and as though

Discussing a film with friends after watching it; plot, director, actor, scene, subtitles, genre; comparing feelings with -сан юм шиг and evidential -жээ; EN: present participle clauses (a man riding a horse, the actress playing the mother)

Visiting a gallery in Ulaanbaatar and talking about paintings and sculpture; canvas, brushstroke, colors, artist, collection, abstract vs traditional; modifying nouns with -сан/-даг participles in descriptive reviews; EN: past participle clauses (a painting created in 1950, works inspired by nature)

Debating how young Mongolian artists mix tradition with pop, rock and hip-hop; heritage, fusion, audience, festival, preserve, innovate; combining comparison with contrast (мэт санагдах, юм шиг харагдах); EN: as if/as though with unreal past (he talked as though he had been there), reduced clauses with -ing for reasons and results

Writing a short review of a concert, film or exhibition for a magazine or website; evaluative vocabulary, recommending, vivid imagery; written style combining -сан юм шиг, -сан мэт and participle modifiers; EN: participle clauses and as if/as though in review writing, avoiding overuse

units.scope: elections, the State Great Khural, public debate; -хын хувьд, -аас гадна, -хын зэрэгцээ; EN: inversion after negative adverbials

lessons.focus: Voting at a polling station on election day; vocabulary: сонгууль, сонгогч, саналын хуудас, санал өгөх, нэр дэвшигч, намууд; grammar: -хын хувьд ('as for, in terms of') to state a position on an issue, and EN: 'Never have I...' as a first look at inversion after negative adverbials

Following a parliamentary session and describing how the legislature works; vocabulary: Улсын Их Хурал, гишүүн, хууль санал болгох, батлах, чуулган, байнгын хороо, засгийн газар; grammar: -аас гадна ('besides, in addition to') to add points in formal reports, and EN: inversion with 'Not only... but also' and 'Only when/after...'

Analyzing candidates' campaign platforms and what they promise; vocabulary: мөрийн хөтөлбөр, амлалт, сурталчилгаа, нэр дэвших, итгэл найдвар, татвар, нийгмийн халамж; grammar: -хын зэрэгцээ ('alongside, while also') to link parallel policy goals, and EN: inversion after 'Hardly/Scarcely... when' and 'No sooner... than'

Taking part in a televised or town-hall debate; vocabulary: маргах, байр суурь, нотлох, шүүмжлэх, эсэргүүцэх, дэмжих, хэлэлцүүлэг; grammar: combining -хын хувьд, -аас гадна and -хын зэрэгцээ to build a structured argument, and EN: inversion with 'Under no circumstances', 'In no way', 'At no point'

Discussing citizen participation, NGOs, petitions and protests; vocabulary: иргэний нийгэм, төрийн бус байгууллага, хүсэлт, жагсаал, ил тод байдал, шийдвэр гаргалт, хариуцлага; grammar: choosing the right connector among -хын хувьд / -аас гадна / -хын зэрэгцээ in nuanced contexts, and EN: inversion with 'Little did', 'Rarely', 'Seldom' for rhetorical effect
